newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-ZURBRIGGEN SURVIVES TEST OF NERVE TO WIN DOWNHILL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ZURBRIGGEN SURVIVES TEST OF NERVE TO WIN DOWNHILL.

text.p: Swiss veteran Heidi Zurbriggen's second career World Cup victory in a downhill on Saturday proved to be a test of her nerve.
Zurbriggen has often been the victim of races which have had to be called off when she was leading or of events when late starters have snatched victory from under her nose.
But on Saturday Zurbriggen could celebrate after she overcame the poor visibility on the 3,010-metre long Strohsack piste to post a winning time of one minute 42.33 seconds.

"Today I was worried the fog would set in again and that the race would have to be interrupted," said Zurbriggen, whose only other win in 12 years on the circuit was in a downhill in Lillehammer, Norway, in 1996.

The race, which was the third attempt in two days to stage a downhill at Bad Kleinkirchheim, was interrupted for 10 minutes after 25 starters. Under World Cup rules, a race result becomes valid only after 30 racers have skied.

Earlier on Saturday, organisers were forced to halt the first of two scheduled downhills after nine racers because of heavy fog. The fog returned during the second downhill to prevent the women with the final 10 bib numbers from starting.
On Friday, a race which was meant to be the replacement for a downhill in December which was called off in Crans Montana, Switzerland, was stopped after seven starters for the same reason.
Three winters ago, Zurbriggen believed she had clinched her maiden victory in a super-G in Altenmarkt, Austria, until the race was declared void a day later because of irregular piste conditons.
"Today in the finish area, I suddenly started thinking about Altenmarkt," said the 29-year-old Zurbriggen. "I felt so relieved when the top 30 were finally down. Only then did I realise I had won.
"I knew I could do well on this slope after my good results in training ," said Zurbriggen, who clocked the fastest time in the second training run on Thursday.
Zurbriggen, younger sister of former world and Olympic champion Pirmin, said a new, harder ski boot which she began using last week had improved her performance dramatically.
"My new boot allows me to corner faster. During tests last week, we discovered I was half a second faster with this boot," she said.
Hilde Gerg was second on Saturday in 1:42.69 for her best downhill result. The German won a super-G at Val d'Isere in December.
Austria's Stefanie Schuster, who joined the World Cup circuit in 1989, was third in 1:43.06 for her first appearance on a World Cup podium.
"It is especially nice to do well at home. I hope I can continue getting good results," said Schuster, who had led in the day's first downhill before it was called off.
Sweden's world and Olympic champion Pernilla Wiberg finished fifth in 1:43.10 to keep her lead in the overall World Cup standings on 763 points.
Her fiercest rival and the defending overall title-holder, Katja Seizinger of Germany, was disappointing in her favourite discipline with 10th place.
Seizinger, the reigning downhill Olympic champion, made a big mistake in the middle section of the slope and only just avoided a fall. She is 174 points behind Wiberg.
The women's circuit continues on Sunday with a super-G on the same slope in Bad Kleinkirchheim.
